blogs.title: From Bite to Death: Preventing Fatal *Capnocytophaga* Sepsis in the Immunocompetent
blogs.description: This post highlights the often-overlooked danger of dog bites in adults, detailing the clinical presentation of *Capnocytophaga canimorsus* sepsis which can mimic other infectious etiologies. It focuses on key warning signs like refractory hypoglycemia and rapid shock in bite management protocols.

blogs.title: The Sepsis-TMA Lag: Why Thrombotic Microangiopathy Reveals Itself After Initial Recovery
blogs.description: A critical analysis of the unique diagnostic window in infection-triggered CM-HUS, where DIC and sepsis initially mask the underlying TMA. The post explores the clinical phenomena where hemolysis and renal failure only manifest after initial fever and inflammatory markers begin to resolve.

blogs.title: Triaging TMA: Using PLASMIC Scores and ADAMTS13 to Avoid TTP Misdiagnosis
blogs.description: Guidelines for rapid differentiation between Thrombotic Thrombocytopenic Purpura (TTP) and Other TMA (like CM-HUS) are discussed. It reviews the utility of clinical scores like PLASMIC to prioritize treatment decisions while waiting for ADAMTS13 activity and complement studies.

blogs.title: Eculizumab vs. Antibiotics: Navigating the Therapeutic Paradox of CM-HUS During Bacteraemia
blogs.description: An in-depth look at the safety dilemma of administering terminal complement inhibitors (eculizumab) to patients with active *Capnocytophaga* or other encapsulated bacterial infections. It addresses the risk of uncontrolled sepsis versus the need for prompt TMA management.

blogs.title: Biopsy or Blindly? Determining the Utility of Renal Biopsy in Acquired TMA Diagnoses
blogs.description: This post evaluates the role of kidney biopsy in adult TMA cases, such as this CM-HUS patient. It discusses indications for invasive testing, the necessity of distinguishing Shiga-toxin vs. Complement-mediated causes, and how pathology findings confirm the diagnosis when serology is inconclusive.

blogs.title: Hereditary or Triggered? Distinguishing Inherited Complement Defects from Infection-Induced TMA
blogs.description: A review of the genetic workup involved in diagnosing Complementary-Mediated HUS. It covers the conditions required to diagnose acquired CM-HUS triggered by infection in the absence of pathogenic complement gene variants found in the patient's study.
